assessment.nobel_worthiness: X-ray free-electron lasers created a new class of intense, ultrashort, tunable X-ray sources, opening experiments on matter at atomic and molecular scales. Their broad impact as research instruments is exceptionally strong.
assessment.attribution: Pellegrini's concepts and accelerator designs, Kim's accelerator physics, and Rossbach's role in realizing the European XFEL span essential contributions. Credit across facilities and teams remains difficult to delimit.
assessment.maturity: The sources have operated for years and enabled a substantial, international body of reproducible science.
uncertainties: The relative weight of foundational designs and later facility construction may complicate a three-person attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP's precision maps established a quantitative picture of the early universe and sharply constrained cosmological parameters. This is a major, durable observational achievement.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page made central contributions to instrument and analysis work, and Spergel helped shape the interpretation of the results. The credit reflects both measurement and scientific synthesis.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been tested against later observations and remain a foundation of precision cosmology.
uncertainties: The discovery rests on a large collaboration, and the boundary between WMAP's contribution and the broader CMB program needs care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks have brought atomic timekeeping to a new level of precision and opened powerful tests of fundamental physics, geodesy, and time standards. The measurement advance is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Katori's lattice clock concept and Ye's leading experimental development represent distinct, complementary advances.
assessment.maturity: Independent groups have demonstrated increasingly precise clocks, though broader adoption and some proposed applications are still developing.
uncertainties: The eventual Nobel scale of impact will depend partly on how far clock comparisons and applications reshape measurement practice.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction showed how reliable information processing can be possible despite the fragility of quantum states, changing the foundations and aims of quantum information physics.
assessment.attribution: Kitaev's topological approach and the independent code and algorithmic advances of Steane and Shor are central, identifiable contributions.
assessment.maturity: Logical qubits and error-correction protocols have been demonstrated, but scaling to sustained, useful fault-tolerant computation remains an active experimental challenge.
uncertainties: It is not yet clear which architectures or error-correction approaches will prove decisive.
The field's ultimate practical reach remains unestablished.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice experiments made controlled studies of strongly interacting quantum matter possible and established quantum simulation as a powerful experimental method.
assessment.attribution: Bloch and Greiner led landmark experimental demonstrations, while Cirac's theory helped establish the platform's purpose and possibilities. The associated theoretical and experimental contributions involve more people than can be recognized.
assessment.maturity: The platform and its methods are mature, with sustained results across multiple systems and research groups.
uncertainties: The distinction between simulation as a method and specific discoveries made with it may affect how the achievement is framed.
Peter Zoller's central theoretical role makes the three-person attribution particularly difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene revealed that a tunable moiré structure can produce correlated electronic phases, creating a major new experimental direction in quantum materials.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat-band mechanism; Jarillo-Herrero's group demonstrated the striking correlated behavior. The theory and experiment are closely linked.
assessment.maturity: The phenomenon has been actively reproduced and studied, but explanations of the range of observed phases remain contested.
uncertainties: It is unsettled how much of the observed phenomenology is specific to this material and how much expresses a general principle.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos established a new observational window on the universe and launched neutrino astronomy at energies inaccessible to conventional telescopes.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was a leading advocate and scientific architect of IceCube, while Karle made major contributions to detector design and construction. The achievement necessarily rests on a large collaboration.
assessment.maturity: The signal is established and follow-up observations have grown, but identifying sources and understanding the population are still ongoing.
uncertainties: The limited number of confidently identified sources makes the field's scientific reach still uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Event Horizon Telescope produced the first resolved images of black-hole shadows, an extraordinary demonstration of global interferometry and a vivid test of strong-gravity predictions.
assessment.attribution: Falcke helped develop the shadow-imaging concept, Moran contributed long-standing expertise in very-long-baseline interferometry, and Doeleman led key technical and observational efforts. The image depended on a broad international collaboration.
assessment.maturity: The observations have been extended to additional targets and epochs, although interpretation continues to rely on modeling of complex accretion flows.
uncertainties: The boundary between the conceptual prediction, the interferometric method, and the collaboration's observations is difficult to represent with three names.
